Title: Stress-activated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 initiates selective nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons.

Hypothesis. In sporadic ALS motor neurons whose dysfunction is driven by TDP-43 proteinopathy, sustained cellular stress activates a kinase that phosphorylates the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 at clustered Ser/Thr sites in or adjacent to its GLFG-repeat region. This phosphorylation increases pore passive permeability and lowers the rate of facilitated NLS-cargo import. The initiating lesion is an intrinsic pore modification; cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing, transport-factor sequestration, Ran-gradient dissipation, and cell death follow as downstream amplifiers. C9orf72-repeat disease [S2] is excluded from this causal claim, although convergence at the level of import failure is permitted.

Causal chain, initiating versus downstream. Initiating: kinase activation → Nup98 GLFG-region phosphorylation → selective loss of facilitated NLS import and increased passive leak. Downstream: reduced nuclear retention of TDP-43 → cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies and phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulation [S3] → stress-granule formation and sequestration of import machinery [S4] → Ran-gradient collapse → cell death. The Ran gradient is deliberately decoupled from the initiation claim and used only as a downstream readout.

Supported premises. [S1] Nuclear-pore and transport components associate with insoluble TDP-43, and pore/transport pathology is present in ALS tissue — co-occurrence, not direction. [S3] Stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies impair import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and recruit or mislocalize transport proteins — the downstream arm invoked here. [S4] Stress-granule assembly sequesters transport factors and impairs transport — the principal competing mechanism, and the reason perturbations must not rely on removing granules alone. [S2] Transport dysfunction exists in the C9orf72 genetic context and is used only to define scope. None of these sources identifies a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as causal.

Speculative bridges (assumptions, no packet support). A1: a stress-activated kinase (p38 or JNK as candidates) phosphorylates Nup98 in adult motor neurons. A2: the relevant residues are 2–3 clustered Ser/Thr sites near GLFG repeats, nominated from mitotic Nup98 phospho-mapping — this sourcing is unverified prior knowledge and must be re-confirmed by mass spectrometry before guiding construct design. A3: phosphorylation precedes TDP-43 egress; the packet only supports co-occurrence. A4: the mechanism is specific to TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS. Phosphomimetic Asp/Glu substitutions are acknowledged as chemically poor phosphate mimics and anchor no conclusion.

Discriminating preclinical test strategy. Model/context: human iPSC-derived motor neurons from sporadic ALS patients with TDP-43 pathology, with isogenic CRISPR-corrected controls; a parallel TDP-43-overexpression neuronal line as a convergent arm. Comparison arms: (i) stressed wild-type, (ii) stressed Nup98 knock-in phospho-null (S→A) at candidate residues, (iii) unstressed phosphomimetic knock-in, (iv) stressed cells expressing dominant-negative p38/JNK, (v) vehicle versus acute kinase-inhibitor additions. Measured outcomes: (a) time-resolved fluorescent NLS-cargo nuclear import rate per nucleus (primary discriminator), (b) baseline passive pore permeability by size-graded dextrans, (c) Nup98 phospho-occupancy at candidate residues by targeted mass spectrometry of immuno-purified pore fractions at hourly intervals, (d) nuclear/cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio and cytoplasmic assembly burden by immunofluorescence, (e) importin-β and Ran sequestration into stress granules, (f) viability. Temporal precedence separates cause from consequence: the hypothesis predicts phospho-occupancy and import decline rise together and precede detectable cytoplasmic TDP-43 aggregation, whereas sequestration-first predicts import loss scales with granule number and importin sequestration regardless of Nup98 phospho-state.

Falsifying observation. The hypothesis is falsified in this model if (i) stressed Nup98 phospho-null knock-in motor neurons show NLS-import kinetics and nuclear TDP-43 retention indistinguishable from stressed wild-type — stress driving the same import loss without Nup98 phosphorylation and with no protection by the null allele, indicating sequestration or another pathway suffices; or (ii) Nup98 phospho-occupancy rises only after cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies are already detectable, reversing the claimed ordering and reclassifying phosphorylation as a consequence.

Limitations. Nup98 phosphorylation is proposed, not established, as an ALS cause; kinase identity and residues are assumptions. Phospho-null alleles may be functionally compensated by other pore components or modifications. iPSC-derived motor neurons may not reproduce adult late-onset biology, and line heterogeneity could obscure cell-specific timing. The claim is scoped to TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS and excludes universal extension to C9orf72 disease [S2], FTD, or all sporadic subgroups.

Argument for the top-ranked item: the packet establishes pore/transport disruption in ALS tissue and two candidate upstream-looking mechanisms [S3] [S4] but leaves direction unresolved. Selecting an intrinsic pore modification as the initiator is the most decisive divergence from sequestration-first alternatives, because a single site-level knock-in plus hourly phospho-mapping can dissociate pore chemistry from granule biology within one experiment. The evidence base is genuine yet incomplete, so promisingness and confidence are kept moderate.

ranking.item: Stress-activated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 initiates selective nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons.
